links.comparator_used: Outputting all summaries without abstention (no withholding of low-groundedness output)
links.effect: Faithfulness improved from 61.7% to 72.6% when the least-grounded 20% of output was withheld
links.tradeoff: 20% of output is withheld and must be reviewed by clinicians
links.quote: For hallucination detection, groundedness scores achieve 0.77 AUROC with the medical-finetuned model: competitive with embedding-based confidence at zero additional cost, and enable an abstention mechanism that improves faithfulness from 61.7% to 72.6% by withholding the least: grounded 20% of output for clinician review.

links.effect: Attention-based groundedness scores reached 0.77 AUROC with the medical-finetuned model, described as competitive with embedding-based confidence at zero additional cost
links.quote: For hallucination detection, groundedness scores achieve 0.77 AUROC with the medical-finetuned model: competitive with embedding-based confidence at zero additional cost, and enable an abstention mechanism that improves faithfulness from 61.7% to 72.6% by withholding the least: grounded 20% of output for clinician review.

links.effect: Medical finetuning reported to substantially improve reliability of attention-based hallucination detection (0.77 AUROC reported for the medical-finetuned model); no numeric comparison given in the abstract
links.quote: Notably, medical finetuning substantially improves the reliability of attention-based hallucination detection, suggesting that domain adaptation produces more semantically structured attention patterns amenable to self-auditing.

design_hint: selective abstention / uncertainty-based filtering for clinician review
